title: Peter Village Enclosure (15Fa166): Early Woodland in Fayette County
summary: In Fayette County, Peter Village is a large ditch-and-embankment earthwork first used around 300–200 BCE, tied to working local galena and barite.
bodyMarkdown:
In Fayette County, Peter Village is a huge, non-geometric ditch-and-embankment earthwork Rafinesque paced as a roughly twenty-sided polygon nearly 3,800 feet around. Early use (~300–200 BCE) looks pre-Adena: a stockade, then ditch and bank, tied to harvesting and working local galena and barite rather than a simple village.

Later Adena people reused the enclosure briefly; recent LiDAR and radiocarbon work suggest it may be among the Middle Ohio Valley’s earliest ditch-and-embankment monuments, with a southern entrance and a second outer embankment still reading in the ground.
Source: [Ancient Monuments of the Mississippi Valley (Squier and Davis, 1848)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Monuments_of_the_Mississippi_Valley)
